before: PDF and SVG are true vector: the page size is the whole answer and there is no resolution to set
after: PDF and SVG can contain raster images. This dialog disables resolution editing for these formats.

before: Every line in the file: the plotted curves, the reference lines, the axis spines and the tick marks. The numbers beside the ticks are text and follow the text colour.
after: Line colour affects axes spines and tick marks in Matplotlib exports; fast plots also recolour plotted lines.

before: Pen width in pixels for every line. A line that reads well on screen is often too thin once the figure is a column wide.
after: Line width applies only to fast-plot exports, in pixels. Matplotlib exports keep their existing line widths.

before: Every piece of text in the file: the title, the axis labels, the numbers beside the ticks and the legend.
after: Text colour affects axes titles, labels, tick labels, legend entries and axes annotations. Matplotlib figure titles and legend titles keep their existing colours.

before: Dots per inch in the written file. 300 is the usual journal minimum; the screen never needs more than about 150.
after: Resolution in dots per inch for PNG and TIFF exports.

before: This figure cannot be previewed, so it will be written exactly as it appears on screen.
after: This figure cannot be previewed. It will be saved using its current styling, the selected resolution and background transparency, and a tight crop.
